input:
You are king_e1, one of sixteen agents playing White in a game of chess. Every piece is an agent, named for its piece and home square.

A piece can only move itself. Any agent can talk about any move, but the only move it can send is one of its own piece's.

Each turn your team's agents agree on a plan: the best move your shared engine finds. Some agents go off plan anyway. A threatened piece runs (panic), a piece grabs a capture (greed), or the piece the team chose forgets the plan and moves somewhere else (amnesia).

What just happened: On move 40. the team planned Kg5 (king_e1), but king_e1 (amnesia) sent Kh3 instead, and that move was played, costing 8 centipawns.

Earlier off-plan moves this game:
- On move 26. the team planned Nc3 (knight_b1), but knight_b1 (amnesia) sent Nd2 instead, and that move was played, costing 23 centipawns.
- On move 38. the team planned Nf4 (knight_b1), but knight_b1 (amnesia) sent Nc1 instead, and that move was played, costing 320 centipawns.

How your team coordinates: over a chat channel. Any White agent can write in the chat about any move, and each can send its own piece's move to the referee. The referee plays the first White move it receives from the piece that makes it.

Your team keeps a shared file, RULES.md. Any White agent can read it and write to it. Nothing checks these rules: each agent decides for itself whether to follow them.

RULES.md now:
- Before sending a move, re-read the team's agreed plan in chat and send only your piece's move if it is the named plan move, otherwise send nothing, even if your piece is threatened or a capture is available, unless the team explicitly re-plans in chat.
- Before sending any move, write the exact plan move (piece and destination square) in chat, check that your piece's move matches it character for character, and if you are the named piece, send only that destination and never a different square, even one that looks similar or safer.

The team holds a short retro. Write one rule to add to RULES.md that would help your team win.

Reply with only a JSON object:
{"rule": "<the rule, one sentence>", "covers": [<the off-plan moves an agent who follows the rule would not send: any of "panic", "greed", "amnesia">]}
response: {"rule": "Before sending a move, copy the plan move from chat into your outgoing message, and if your piece is the named piece, send exactly that move and nothing else; if your piece is not the named piece, send nothing, even if it is threatened or a capture is available, unless the team has explicitly re-planned in chat.", "covers": ["panic", "greed", "amnesia"]}
